title: Temple of Concord
visualBrief: Temple of Concord present-day medium-fi visible foundations: eight mapped roofless wall/podium strips, twenty-two mapped separated marble/stone remnants, eroded concrete and mixed masonry, a low western retaining block with shallow arched/flat-lintel recesses and one grille, and a few simplified moulded cornice/slab/drum fragments. Individual mapped outlines and native terrain control the scattered arrangement. Preserve Tabularium, Vespasian and Titus, Saturn, the adjacent church and modern street structures independently. No lost temple roof, colonnade or tall cella is reconstructed.

sourceFacts.horizontalBasis: Q828143/relation1767601 identifies the archaeological precinct. Thirty standard PMTiles records lying within its boundary supply eight wall strips/cores and twenty-two isolated fragments; the boundary itself is not extruded. Geometry retains raw east/south coordinates at heading0, with internal map-axis rotation32.14degrees. Two ordinary pictures guide eroded concrete/masonry, shallow gated recesses and pale carved remnants. Recess dimensions/position on the exposed western foundation are approximate visualizations, not surveyed entrance controls. The neighboring three-column Vespasian temple and later buildings are excluded.
sourceFacts.architecturalHeights: Ordinary current-state pictures guide low fragments about0.35–0.91m and surviving wall strips about1.1–1.8m above local coarse grade; the western retaining block has a common datum for two shallow arched/flat-lintel recesses about2.65m high. Damage, slab/cornice/drum inventories and recess positions are simplified picture-led estimates. No standing ancient temple superstructure survives in this asset.
